basics.name: Yifan Jing（敬益凡）
basics.summary: Undergraduate Data Science student at the University of Michigan, expected to graduate in 2027. Research interests include multimodal reasoning, LLM reasoning, AI scientist systems, and AI evaluation.

highlights: Investigating multimodal reasoning through systematic evaluations and controlled ablations; a manuscript is under review at ICLR 2027 (title withheld).
Developing AI scientist systems and self-evolving agents that autonomously propose, evaluate, and iteratively improve reasoning strategies and scientific solutions.

work.summary: Developing mathematical discovery and formal reasoning tasks for evaluating frontier AI agents.
highlights: 1 task accepted for inclusion: Cambrian projection in Lean 4, with domain, technical, and final review approved as of September 22, 2026.
Built a complete reference proof and isolated verifier for Reading's maximality theorem on arbitrary Coxeter systems.
Developed HintFlow, training a 4B language-model policy to guide frozen 14B–20B reasoning models through selective supervised fine-tuning and a modified GRPO objective.
Built the end-to-end training and inference pipeline using Qwen3, GPT-OSS-20B, LoRA, and vLLM.

work.summary: Contact Sensing Hexapod. Advisor: Prof. Shai Revzen. Simulation contributor to arXiv:2603.09147.
highlights: Developed large-scale MuJoCo simulations for multi-legged locomotion, evaluating modular controllers across varying morphologies and irregular terrain conditions.
Developing an efficient control pipeline that uses LLM-guided search to distill a high-capacity neural policy into an interpretable finite-state machine.

work.summary: Hybrid Transformer analysis on the Associative Recall problem. Mentor: Dr. Samet Oymak.
Completed Translation-Invariant Total Orders (TITO) research. Advisor: Dr. Grant Barkley.
highlights: Formalized order-comparability through inversion sets and implemented weak order comparison, joins, normalization, and visualization in SageMath.
Released the TITO_Explore SageMath package and arXiv:2607.11709; targeting FPSAC 2027.

work.summary: ThinkAct LLM Agent with self-reflection and self-consistency. Mentor: Dr. Samet Oymak.

publications.summary: Multimodal reasoning research at Princeton University.

publications.name: Computing Tools for Translation-Invariant Total Orders
publications.summary: Yifan Jing, Emma Yicheng Lou, Shaotian Sun, and Yuxuan Wu. SageMath tools for weak order comparison, joins, normalization, and visualization. Targeting FPSAC 2027.

teaching.description: Lectured 125+ students; taught Java in office hours, recitations, and exam prep.

portfolio.name: AI-Assisted Discovery — Pure-Loss Converse Counterexample
portfolio.description: With Yue Tu and six parallel AI agents, constructed a general family of counterexamples to a candidate pure-loss second-order converse and verified the disproof in Lean 4. The candidate arose from a question posed by Mark M. Wilde, Joseph M. Renes, and Saikat Guha in 2014, 12 years earlier. QIQCOP credits Yue Tu and Yifan Jing and lists the problem as solved.
